CASE STUDY 01

NEXUS, a multi-tenant SaaS where no organization can see another’s data

Businesses want one place for customers, orders and invoices, and each company’s data must stay strictly separate. NEXUS enforces that isolation in the query layer, so it cannot be forgotten inside a view.

Public, MIT license, CI on every push

BACKEND LAYERS · ONE DIRECTION

Every app follows the same layering, so tenant scoping lives in one place

models
Schema, validation, constraints and indexes.
selectors
Read paths. The only place tenant scoping is written.
services
Write paths. Atomic, enforce the invariants.
permissions
Reusable classes: may this actor do this?
serializers
Input parsing and output shape.
views
Thin HTTP glue. One selector or service call.

THE CODE BEHIND THE 404

Tenant scoping is written once

Every read of invoices goes through this selector, so a record from another organization is simply not found and the API answers 404. Services and API code never query the model directly.

backend/apps/invoices/selectors.py · trimmed
def invoices_for_user(user: User) -> QuerySet[Invoice]: return Invoice.objects.filter( organization__memberships__user=user ).select_related("organization", "customer", "order") def invoice_for_user(user: User, invoice_id: int) -> Invoice | None: return invoices_for_user(user).filter(pk=invoice_id).first()
TENANCY

One user, several organizations

A user can belong to many organizations and switch between them. Customers, orders, invoices and the dashboard are scoped to the active one.

ROLES

Owner, admin, member

Any member can read. Only owners and admins can write, and the owner is protected. Tenant isolation and roles are tested as explicit properties.

WORKFLOW

Customers, orders, invoices

Orders move through a status workflow. Invoices are auto-numbered per organization (INV-0001), with overdue highlighting and a management command for the sweep.

DASHBOARD

An overview from two endpoints

One aggregation endpoint for the headline totals and one for the daily series behind the 30 and 90 day charts.

SECURITY

Short-lived tokens, fail-fast config

15-minute access tokens held in memory, refresh tokens blacklisted on logout, a non-root container, and production settings that refuse to start without secrets.

PRODUCTION

One compose command to run it

PostgreSQL, Gunicorn and nginx, health probes, structured JSON logs with request IDs, and an end-to-end smoke test in CI.
